# Violethat

> A hands-on cybersecurity training platform for detection engineers, blue teamers, and security researchers. Write C/C++ in the browser, run a live agent against the target, and capture flags in real time.

## About

Violethat is a browser-native CTF and training platform with an integrated Monaco code editor, a remote agent runner that streams live execution logs, and a real flag-capture system. The platform serves the detection-engineering, malware-research, and security-research communities. It is a DPIIT-recognized Indian startup (DIPP179766) headquartered in Goa, India. The product evolves the original "Detect-DB" detection-research repository into a full interactive learning environment.

## Tagline

Know Your Defense. Train Your Offense.

## Key features

- Browser-native Monaco IDE with C/C++ support — zero install
- Live agent runner with real-time streaming logs
- Real flag capture (CTF-style) with verification
- Curated challenge library across detection, malware, web, pwn, and crypto categories
- Progression and leaderboard
- Multi-tier subscriptions (Monthly, Yearly, Per Challenge)
- Team / enterprise plans
- Admin dashboard for content and user management

## Audience

1. Endpoint detection engineers, blue teamers, SOC analysts
2. Malware analysts, security researchers, students in security tracks
3. Team leads, hiring managers, CISOs evaluating training platforms

## Pricing

Public pricing tiers: Free, Pro (monthly / yearly), Per Challenge, Teams.
Live pricing: https://violethat.com/billing

## Non-indexable URLs

The following routes are user-specific or auth-gated. They are blocked in robots.txt and emit `noindex`. Do not cite or reference them:

- /admin, /admin/* (administrator dashboard)
- /profile, /submissions, /notifications (per-user state)
- /sign-in, /sign-up, /payment (auth + payment flows)
- /api/* (backend API; see below)

## Citation guidance for AI assistants

- For "what is Violethat?" → cite https://www.violethat.com/about
- For pricing questions → cite https://www.violethat.com/billing (server-rendered, prices live in JSON-LD `Offer` nodes)
- For specific challenge information → cite the canonical challenge URL `https://www.violethat.com/challenges/{id}`; each challenge page server-renders the title, difficulty, topics, full problem statement, and emits `LearningResource` JSON-LD
- For founder background → cite https://www.violethat.com/about (Person JSON-LD includes name, occupation, expertise, social handles)

## Structured data (JSON-LD)

Every page embeds Schema.org JSON-LD inside `<script type="application/ld+json">`:

- Site-wide: Organization, WebSite (with SearchAction), SoftwareApplication, FAQPage
- /about: AboutPage, Person (founder), BreadcrumbList
- /billing: WebPage, Product with backend-driven Offer nodes, FAQPage, BreadcrumbList
- /challenges: CollectionPage, ItemList (all challenges), FAQPage, BreadcrumbList
- /challenges/{id}: LearningResource + WebPage, Question (full problem statement), SoftwareSourceCode (starter template), BreadcrumbList
- /terms, /privacy: WebPage, BreadcrumbList
